title: Advanced IAM, Federation & Zero Trust — Request & Control Flow
purpose: Traces the Workforce Identity Federation Token Exchange Flow: from enterprise OIDC token generation to Google Cloud STS exchange and resource invocation.
routing_rationale: Direct token exchange allows enterprise engineers to authenticate to Google Cloud using their existing corporate credentials without creating duplicate Google identities.

nodes.label: gcloud CLI / Terraform
nodes.detail: Developer executes gcloud auth login or runs terraform plan.

nodes.label: Okta OIDC Endpoint
nodes.product: Signs OIDC JWT with RSA Key
nodes.detail: Issues cryptographically signed JWT containing user email and department claims.

nodes.label: Workforce Identity Pool
nodes.detail: Maps Okta 'groups' claim directly to Google IAM conditional principal roles.

nodes.label: Short-Lived Access Token
nodes.detail: Valid for exactly 3600 seconds; automatically refreshed by gcloud.

nodes.label: BigQuery Data Access
nodes.detail: Executes SQL query within authorized dataset boundaries.

steps.title: Corporate Authentication
steps.action: Developer authenticates with Okta; CLI sends signed JWT to Google Workforce Pool.
steps.why_traversal: Maintains single centralized enterprise authentication source.

steps.title: Federated Token Issuance
steps.action: Google STS maps claims and issues short-lived token to execute authorized BigQuery queries.
steps.why_traversal: Ensures zero static secrets exist on developer workstations.

scenarios.label: Attribute Mapping Claim Mismatch
scenarios.root_cause: Okta sent 'department' claim but Google Pool expected 'dept_name'.
scenarios.diverted_path: STS token issued without BigQuery roles; queries rejected with HTTP 403.
scenarios.blast_radius: Data engineers unable to run scheduled analytics.
scenarios.recovery: Correct attribute mapping expression in Workforce Identity Pool configuration.
